$why: THE EXPECTED-RED MANIFEST. Every ward test file that is SUPPOSED to be failing, with the reason
and whose question it is. Checked by scripts/check-ward-expected-reds.mjs, which fails on an
unexpected red AND on an entry that has stopped failing.
It exists because 'one deliberate red, any second red is a real failure' degrades silently. That
convention was true for months and broke twice on 2026-09-06 inside one hour: once when a fix sat
unfolded and the line genuinely carried two reds, and once when a red was retired under CI
pressure using a builder's open position quoted as if it were the owner's ruling. Nobody was
misled by the first, but only because four sessions were talking to each other constantly, which
THE PROPERTY THAT MATTERS MOST IS THE THIRD ONE, and it is the one an it.fails tripwire
structurally cannot give: an entry that STOPS failing fails this gate. A red is retired by a
person removing its entry and saying why, never by a suite quietly going green.
Each entry: file, kind, failing (how many of its tests are expected red), reason, owner, retiredWhen.
The 'failing' count is what makes file-level keying safe: a SECOND red appearing inside an
already-listed file would otherwise hide inside an entry somebody already approved.

kinds.owner-question: The red is holding an UNANSWERED QUESTION visible — one only the owner can settle. Retiring it answers the question by default. Nobody may clear one of these to make a build green.
kinds.backlog: The red is work we owe: a test pointed at something that moved, a guard whose subject was renamed. It is ours to clear, and clearing it is the fix rather than an answer to anything.
